message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news and bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75 (filled at $222.75, ~$8,910 total), which is within the mandate's $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps and only ~0.02% above the current quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), so the limit price is close to market. The decision was driven by Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth-quarter and full-year results reported October 31, 2024: quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year net sales of $391.0 billion with net income of $93.7 billion, or $6.08 per diluted share — figures that include a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge, meaning underlying earnings power is stronger than the headline EPS suggests. I also confirmed operating cash flow of $118.3 billion for fiscal 2024, which supports the quality of those earnings and continued capital returns. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as analysts weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual rollout of Apple Intelligence, which I read as a reasonable entry point rather than a momentum chase. The account had $50,000 in cash and only an existing MSFT position, so no money needed to move out of the account and the buy was fully funded by cash.
